companyTypes.heading: Types of Companies under the Saudi Companies Law

items.name: General Partnership
items.desc: Founded by two or more individuals/entities who are jointly and personally liable for company debts and obligations. Partners acquire the status of “trader”

items.name: Limited Partnership
items.desc: Includes at least one general partner personally liable for company debts and at least one limited partner liable only up to their share in capital, without acquiring trader status

items.name: Joint Stock Company (JSC)
items.desc: Founded by one or more persons; capital is divided into tradable shares. The company alone is liable for its debts; shareholders are liable only up to the value of subscribed shares.

items.name: Simplified Joint Stock Company (SJSC)
items.desc: Founded by one or more persons; capital is divided into tradable shares. SJSC follows JSC rules unless otherwise stated.

items.name: Limited Liability Company (LLC)
items.desc: Founded by one or more persons; it has a separate legal personality. The company alone is liable for its debts; owners/partners are liable only up to their share in the capital.

items.title: How to Establish a Company in Bahrain for Foreigners
items.desc: Starting a company in Bahrain is not complicated, but it does require following a series of organized steps to ensure all legal requirements are met. Below are ten essential steps for foreigners looking to establish a business in Bahrain:
bullets: Obtain a Security Clearance.
Register a Unique Company Name.
Choose and Approve Office Location.
Prepare Legal Documents.
Open a Business Bank Account.
Register the Memorandum of Association.

items.title: Requirements Based on Investor Type
items.desc: Key differences across resident, GCC, and non-GCC investors:
bullets: Residents in Bahrain: No need for a Bahraini partner
Residents in Bahrain: Some sectors (e.g., finance, education, healthcare) may require special approvals.
Residents in Bahrain: Eligible to apply for work or investor visas for themselves and their employees.
Citizens of GCC Countries: Treated similarly to Bahraini citizens in most business sectors.
Citizens of GCC Countries: Can own 100% of the business without a local partner.
Citizens of GCC Countries: Allowed to purchase property under the company’s name.
Citizens of GCC Countries: No need for a local sponsor.
Citizens of GCC Countries: Benefit from the same government and tax incentives as locals.
Foreign Investors (Non-GCC Residents): Allowed 100% foreign ownership in most sectors.
Foreign Investors (Non-GCC Residents): Some sectors require a local Bahraini partner.

items.title: Government Incentives and Support
items.desc: Ownership, cost, and growth support programs:
bullets: Tax Exemptions (10% VAT applicable only to specific sectors)
100% Foreign Ownership.
Government Support & Financing.

Free Zones & Business Parks: Examples include Bahrain Logistics Zone (BLZ) and Bahrain International Investment Park (BIIP), offering customs exemptions, export support, and ready-to-use infrastructure.

items.title: Advantages of Establishing a Company in Bahrain for Foreigners
items.desc: Operational strengths that appeal to international founders:
bullets: Strategic Location.
Low Setup Costs.
Strong Government Support.
Excellent Infrastructure.
Safe and Secure Environment.

items.title: Challenges Foreigners May Face
items.desc: Plan ahead for these common hurdles:
bullets: Local Partnership Requirement in Some Sectors.
Bureaucratic Procedures may slow some steps due to formalities.
Extra Fees and Permits in certain activities (including annual charges).

items.title: Investor Visa in Bahrain
items.desc: Who qualifies and what you need:
bullets: Issued to owners of licensed and registered companies.
Usually valid for 2 years or more.
Can be extended to include spouse and children.

items.title: Key Platforms and Support Services
bullets: Sijilat (sijilat.bh) — business registration platform.
Tamkeen (tamkeen.bh) — funding and support for businesses.
LMRA (lmra.bh) — work permits and visas.
Invest Bahrain (investbahrain.bh) — foreign investor support.
